record_body:
ACCOUNT SNAPSHOT
- Segment: multi-hospital provider network + affiliated clinics (enterprise). Central platform team supports clinical data products and contact center tooling.
- Primary pain: they have multiple LLM pilots blocked by PHI constraints + inconsistent latency/cost when they test on general-purpose APIs.
- Why Redwood: "Private deployment story" + measurable perf/cost controls (batching/caching/routing) + auditability. They want a clear Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private migration path, but expect to start with Private/VPC for PHI.

CURRENT STAGE (Evaluation)
- They are in evaluation planning for a 2–3 week Private/VPC POC with synthetic data first, then a limited PHI slice if security sign-off is clean.
- Internal success criteria is split:
  - Platform Eng: VPC networking works, stable p95 latency, observability/audit hooks, SSO.
  - Clinical/Operations: summarization quality is acceptable and outputs are traceable/defensible (basic eval set + human review).

USE CASES (HEALTHCARE)
1) Clinical summarization (highest priority)
- Inputs: encounter notes + labs + problem list (PHI).
- Output: short summary + problem-focused bullets + "open items" list for care team.
- Usage pattern: async batch (nightly) + on-demand during transitions of care.
- Volume guess: 2–5M notes/month across network (they will confirm).

2) Chart search / clinical Q&A (embeddings + reranking)
- Goal: let clinicians search across policies/protocols + internal knowledge base + patient chart snippets.
- Needs: low-latency retrieval pipeline; can tolerate slightly higher LLM latency if retrieval is fast.

3) Contact center / nurse line summarization
- Call transcript summarization + disposition.
- Some calls include PHI; want same private boundary.

TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS (as captured so far)
- Deployment: Private in their cloud VPC (initially AWS). They asked about on-prem as a longer-term option for specific hospital groups; not in scope for first POC.
- Networking: VPC peering preferred; private DNS; strict egress allowlist. TLS requirements: customer-managed certs acceptable; wants clarity on who terminates TLS where.
- Performance targets (rough):
  - Retrieval/search endpoint p95 < 800ms end-to-end (excluding UI).
  - Summarization can be slower; they cited p95 < 8–12s for typical note sizes, with predictable throughput for batch windows.
- Model flexibility: open to Redwood-recommended model(s) as long as they can pin versions + have rollback/fallback options.
- Routing/fallback: wants policy-based routing (cost vs latency) and an explicit "no cross-region" rule for PHI.

SECURITY / COMPLIANCE NOTES (PHI)
- Residency: US-only for PHI workflows. (They asked if region pinning is enforced at the routing layer.)
- Retention requirements:
  - Strong preference: do not store prompts/outputs by default for PHI workflows.
  - Operational logs allowed if they do not contain PHI; customer wants controls and a written stance.
  - Audit logs: need export to their SIEM with 1-year retention on their side; asked if Redwood can generate admin/action audit events (access, config changes, auth events).
- Encryption/KMS: expects customer-managed keys in Private deployment. Asked about KMS integration points and whether keys can be fully customer-owned.
- Identity: SSO/SAML required; role-based access for console + API keys. They asked for separation of duties (read-only vs admin) for audit.
- Questionnaire posture: wants SOC 2 report under NDA; also asked "Do you sign a BAA?" (flagged for legal; we should not imply current standard terms).

RECENT ACTIVITY TIMELINE
- 2026-01-28: Technical deep dive (Fireflies: ff_2026-01-28_summit_provider_technical_deep_dive)
  - Topics: Private/VPC reference architecture, VPC networking assumptions, logging/SIEM export formats, sizing questions.
  - Key quote: "We can get internal approval if we can show PHI stays inside our VPC and we control retention."
- 2026-01-29: Follow-up email thread (thread_20260129_summit_provider_arch_questions)
  - Asked detailed questions on VPC peering, DNS/TLS assumptions, SIEM export formats.
- 2026-02-06: Internal note (SE): they are sensitive to anything that sounds like prompts/outputs are stored; needs tight language aligned with Security/GRC.
- 2026-02-18: Owner update: confirmed they want to proceed with evaluation, pending a security review call and written retention stance.

OPEN QUESTIONS (to resolve in next 7–10 days)
- Retention controls: confirm exactly what Redwood stores in Private deployment (operational metrics vs request payloads), and how to configure/disable any retention.
- Audit log coverage: what events are available today (admin actions, auth events, key usage, model/version changes) and export mechanism.
- BAA: confirm Redwood position + escalation path for healthcare legal/procurement.
- POC data: confirm whether synthetic-only is acceptable for week 1; define criteria to allow limited PHI.

NEXT STEPS / ACTION ITEMS
- Hannah (AE): send Healthcare security FAQ addendum + reference architecture; propose dates for security review; align on POC commercial guardrails.
- Fatima (SE): provide draft POC plan w/ sizing assumptions + success metrics; clarify KMS and SIEM export implementation details.
- Security (Aisha/Olga): approve customer-facing retention/audit language for this account; prep SOC2 sharing process under NDA.

INTERNAL NOTES
- This is a good fit for the vertical ABM pilot: clear regulated driver, strong Private requirement, and multiple production use cases if first one lands.
- Watch-outs: do not over-promise on BAA or specific certifications beyond what Security/GRC has approved; keep phrasing consistent with the healthcare security FAQ addendum.
